- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out the peak.  
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d forecast), model underestimates mean reversion toward historical range; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of range if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.4), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (e.g., >75% above recent high or <5% below recent low) unless sentiment strongly supports it — otherwise, cap or floor forecasts to avoid overconfidence.
